title: About
text:
This website demonstrates working with Apache Parquet files using PySpark.



Spark Session: Creates a Spark session with the appName “ParquetPenguinsDemo”
Data Loading: Loads the Palmer Penguins dataset
Data Cleaning: Drops all NA values from the dataset
Data Display: Shows the top 10 rows of the cleaned data
Schema Display: Displays the DataFrame schema





Quarto: For creating the static website
PySpark: For data processing
Palmer Penguins: Sample dataset for demonstration
GitHub Actions: For automated deployment




Apache Parquet is a columnar storage file format that is optimized for use with big data processing frameworks. It provides efficient data compression and encoding schemes.

title: Penguins Analytics Example - Summary
text:
This project demonstrates a complete data analytics workflow using Apache Parquet format with PySpark, showcasing data loading, processing, analytics, and visualization.





A comprehensive Python script that: - Loads the Palmer Penguins dataset from Seaborn - Converts data to PySpark DataFrame - Saves data in Parquet format (columnar storage) - Loads and processes Parquet data using PySpark - Performs multiple analytics operations: - Average measurements by species - Distribution by species and island - Sex distribution analysis - Generates visualizations (static and interactive) - Saves analytics results back to Parquet



A helper script that demonstrates: - Reading Parquet files with PySpark - Displaying data and schema - Running queries on Parquet data - Best practices for working with Parquet files



All necessary Python packages: - PySpark 3.5.0 - Distributed data processing - Pandas 2.1.4 - Data manipulation - PyArrow 14.0.2 - Parquet file support - Seaborn 0.13.1 - Statistical visualizations - Matplotlib 3.8.2 - Plotting library - Plotly 5.18.0 - Interactive visualizations



Comprehensive documentation including: - Project overview and features - Installation instructions - Usage examples - Output file descriptions - Information about Parquet format - Dataset description - Technologies used



Properly configured to exclude: - Python artifacts (__pycache__, .pyc) - Data files (*.parquet, *.csv) - Output directories - IDE and OS files - Spark metadata







data/penguins.parquet - Original dataset in Parquet format
data/species_averages.parquet - Aggregated statistics by species
data/species_island_distribution.parquet - Distribution data





output/bill_dimensions_seaborn.png - Scatter plot of bill dimensions by species
output/body_mass_distribution_seaborn.png - Box plot of body mass by species and sex
output/3d_scatter_plotly.html - Interactive 3D scatter plot
output/species_by_island_plotly.html - Interactive bar chart of species distribution








Columnar Storage: Efficient compression and query performance
Schema Evolution: Self-describing format with embedded schema
Cross-Platform: Compatible with Spark, Pandas, and other tools
Compression: Snappy compression reduces file size





DataFrame creation from Pandas
Parquet read/write operations
Data aggregations and grouping
Statistical calculations
Filtering and transformations





Species-level statistics (average measurements)
Geographic distribution analysis (species by island)
Demographic analysis (sex distribution)
Custom queries and filtering





Static plots with Seaborn (publication-ready)
Interactive plots with Plotly (exploratory analysis)
Multiple chart types (scatter, box, 3D scatter, bar)






Install dependencies:
pip install -r requirements.txt
Run the main analytics script:
python penguins_analytics.py
(Optional) Read and query Parquet files:
python read_parquet_example.py
View visualizations:

Open .png files with any image viewer
Open .html files in a web browser for interactive charts






Minimal Dependencies: Only essential packages included
Clean Code: Well-documented with clear structure
Error Handling: Properly handles null values
Performance: Uses Spark’s distributed processing capabilities
Best Practices: Follows PySpark and data engineering conventions
Reproducible: Complete workflow from raw data to insights




Palmer Penguins Dataset - 344 observations of 3 penguin species - 7 variables (species, island, measurements, sex) - Species: Adelie, Chinstrap, Gentoo - Islands: Biscoe, Dream, Torgersen - Measurements: Bill length/depth, flipper length, body mass



✅ Successfully loads data from multiple sources ✅ Converts between formats (CSV → Parquet) ✅ Performs distributed processing with PySpark ✅ Generates meaningful analytics and insights ✅ Creates professional visualizations ✅ Demonstrates Parquet format advantages ✅ Provides reusable, well-documented code ✅ Includes comprehensive documentation

title: Parquet Penguins Demo
text:
This demo shows how to work with the Palmer Penguins dataset using PySpark and Apache Parquet format.

# Import required libraries
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from palmerpenguins import load_penguins

# Create Spark session with the appName ParquetPenguinsDemo
spark = SparkSession.builder \
    .appName("ParquetPenguinsDemo") \
    .master("local[*]") \
    .getOrCreate()

# Load the penguins dataset
penguins_pandas = load_penguins()

# Create a Spark DataFrame from the pandas DataFrame
penguins_df = spark.createDataFrame(penguins_pandas)

# Drop all NA values
penguins_cleaned = penguins_df.dropna()

# Show the top 10 rows
print("Top 10 rows of the cleaned penguins dataset:")
penguins_cleaned.show(10)

# Show the schema
print("\nSchema of the penguins DataFrame:")
penguins_cleaned.printSchema()

# Stop the Spark session
spark.stop()
